bib.title: LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding

question: How well do LLMs understand long contexts across diverse realistic tasks and two languages, and do context-extension and compression methods help?
contributions: LongBench: first bilingual multitask long-context benchmark, 21 datasets, 6 categories, standardized format with automatic metrics
LongBench-E: length-balanced subset (0-4k, 4k-8k, 8k+) for length-vs-performance analysis
Evaluation of 8 LLMs plus analysis of retrieval and summarization compression and memorisation

method.summary: Collects or builds 21 long-context datasets (single/multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot, synthetic, code) in English and Chinese, evaluates 8 LLMs zero-shot with greedy decoding and middle truncation, and studies retrieval and summary compression and no-context memorisation.

datasets.name: LongBench
datasets.size: 4,750 test instances, 21 datasets (Single-doc QA 750, Multi-doc QA 800, Summarization 600, Few-shot 800, Synthetic 600, Code 1000)
datasets.split: test sets of public datasets (VCSUM excepted, insufficient test data); random sampling keeps natural length distribution
datasets.source: NarrativeQA, Qasper, MultiFieldQA-en/zh (authors), HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, DuReader, GovReport, QMSum, MultiNews, VCSUM, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, LSHT, PassageCount/Retrieval-en/zh (authors), LCC, RepoBench-P
datasets.preprocessing: Multi-doc QA: supporting passages plus distractors up to max length, shuffled; DuReader padded to 20 docs. Few-shot: random number of shots per item (TREC [100,600], LSHT [10,40], SAMSum [10,100], TriviaQA [2,24]). PassageRetrieval: 30 passages, one summarised by GPT-3.5-Turbo. PassageCount: M in [17,50] passages, N in [2,M] unique. TriviaQA passages under 1,000 words filtered.

models.name: ChatGLM2-6B-32k
models.init_from: ChatGLM2-6B (32k context in alignment, position interpolation)

inference.samples: single run per item, greedy; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: Zero-shot per-dataset template with instruction at both start and end of prompt (Appendix B); few-shot examples are part of the context; chat templates omitted for few-shot and code tasks
inference.retrieval: Context split into chunks of M words (characters for Chinese), top-N by cosine similarity concatenated as compressed context; chunk 200 x top-7 or 500 x top-3; retrievers ada-002, Contriever, BM25; QA tasks only

parameters.truncation: when L > M, keep first floor(M/2) and last floor(M/2) tokens (middle removed)
parameters.summary_compression: model summarises each chunk, summaries concatenated; summarization tasks only; chunk size not stated for summary
parameters.answer_extraction: few-shot: first line of response; code: first non-comment line

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: n-gram F1 for QA and TriviaQA

metrics.name: Overall
metrics.definition: macro-average of category Avg over 6 categories, for EN, ZH, All (code in both)

baselines: 8 evaluated models; no-retrieval and no-context ablations
eval.protocol: Single greedy run; no significance tests or seeds stated; LongBench-E macro-avg per length bin.

results.claim: Delta score (with minus without context) is proposed as a long-context understanding indicator
Synthetic tasks discriminate strongly (models near-zero or high); summarization and code do not discriminate

limits: Automatic metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) may not reflect response quality and underestimate models with longer responses (authors)
Performance is coupled with instruction-following ability (authors)
Only 8 models, mostly 7B open models and GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k, all dated 2023; none exceed 32k
Retrieval study covers QA tasks only; summarization compression only summarization tasks; single run, no variance reported
Wikipedia-derived tasks show memorisation (no-context scores high), so they partly measure parametric knowledge
Summarization and code tasks discriminate weakly; PassageCount near random for most models
Chinese tasks have length in characters, not comparable to English words

terms.definition: original score minus the score when context is absent; an indicator of long context understanding
